We need propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need to output JSON route with type mol, children reactions etc. Need to identify three steps: likely disconnection: amide formation (C=O to amide), Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid, sulfonamide formation.

So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide bond between C(=O)N and aromatic amine (aniline). So precursor: acid (α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's step 1 (amide formation forward). So retrosynthetic step: target -> precursors: (E)-cinnamoyl aniline? Actually the unsaturated acid is /C=C/C(=O)N... Wait target has C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So forward: carboxylic acid + aniline -> amide. So retrosynthetic: break amide to give acid (with double bond) and aniline.

Next, the unsaturated acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. The acid part is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group via aromatic ring: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring (para). So we can disconnect the double bond formation: break C=C to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid. That's step 2 (Doebner).

Third, sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride reacting with an aniline (the first phenyl ring with methyl). So break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the methyl phenyl amine). So step 3.

Thus route: target -> step1 amide disconnection -> gives unsaturated acid (with phenyl sulfonyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then step2 Doebner -> gives aldehyde (para-methyl phenyl? Wait the aldehyde is on the phenyl attached to sulfonyl). Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring that also has sulfonyl group attached to other phenyl. The aldehyde precursor is that phenyl ring with sulfonyl attached and CHO para? The sulfonyl is attached at position where? In target: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So sulfonamide attaches to phenyl ring (c2ccc...cc2). The aldehyde would be same phenyl with CHO at the position of the double bond (para to sulfonyl). So step2 yields that aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonyl chloride from that phenyl (with CHO?) Actually sulfonyl chloride is derived from same phenyl ring (c1ccc(N)??). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the first phenyl ring (with methyl). The sulfonamide formation is between that phenyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (p-sulfonyl). Wait the sulfonamide in target: NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the nitrogen attached to sulfonyl is from the first phenyl (p-toluidine). So sulfonyl chloride precursor is the sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (c2ccc...cc2) with SO2Cl. So step3: break S-N to give p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO? Actually the sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl with aldehyde substituent). So final precursors: p-toluidine, sulfonyl chloride (Ar-CH=CH-CO2H? Wait after step2 we have aldehyde, not acid). The sulfonyl chloride precursor after step2 would be the same phenyl with aldehyde and SO2Cl.

Thus final three precursors: p-toluidine, aromatic aldehyde (Ar-CHO), malonic acid. That's plausible.
